statement:
Let $H(n,3)$ be the Hamming graph on ${\mathbb Z}_3^n$, and let $U\subseteq {\mathbb Z}_3^n$ induce a subgraph of maximum degree $1$. Write $\alpha(H(n,3))$ for the independence number of $H(n,3)$.

**Ansensio–García-Marco–Knauer conjecture.** All such subsets satisfy

$$
|U|=\alpha(H(n,3))+O(1).
$$

The paper proves several bounds under additional hypotheses, including $|U|\leq \alpha(H(n,3))+729$ when $U$ is $i$-saturated for some $i\in[n]$. The conjecture asks whether a bounded additive error remains valid without any saturation assumption; this remains open.
title: Ansensio–García-Marco–Knauer conjecture on induced degree-one subsets of the ternary Hamming graph
source_references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15004

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).
technical_disposition: The literal equality for every degree-at-most-one subset fails for U empty as n grows; the intended uniform upper bound is distinct. Do not earn credit from the missing inequality. The unsaturated upper-bound problem has no full route here.

statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be integers with $1\leq q\leq p$, and let $\gamma$ be the largest root of

$$
x^2-px-q.
$$

The van der Corput sequence in base $\gamma$ is **completely quasi-equidistributed** in base $(p+1)$ if, for every finite-dimensional truncation of the sequence and every multi-index $\mathbf{k}\in\mathbb{N}_0^d$, its pair-correlation quantity satisfies $C_{(p+1)}(\mathbf{k};P_N)\leq 1$.

**Complete quasi-equidistribution conjecture.** Let $\gamma$ be the largest root of the polynomial $x^2-px-q$ for $1\leq q\leq p$. The van der Corput sequence in base $\gamma$ is c.q.e. in base $(p+1)$.

This conjecture proposes a scrambling base for coordinates associated with an irrational base and is motivated by numerical investigation. The source gives no proof or resolution.
title: Complete quasi-equidistribution conjecture for van der Corput sequences in irrational bases
source_references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15799

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).
technical_disposition: All p,q and every dimension/multi-index are quantified. Finite pair-correlation tests cannot establish complete quasi-equidistribution; the correlation definition and irrational-base truncation rules need the primary body.

statement:
Let $F$ be a forest of order $n\geq 12$, let $P_n$ denote the path on $n$ vertices, and let $[P_3,P_3,P_{n-7}]$ denote the tree formed by joining one endpoint of each of three paths of the indicated orders at a common branching vertex. **The second-largest $Z_1$ conjecture.** Among all forests $F\neq P_n$ of order $n\geq 12$, 
$$
Z_1(F)\leq Z_1([P_3,P_3,P_{n-7}]),
$$
 with equality if and only if $F$ is $[P_3,P_3,P_{n-7}]$. The claim is motivated by computational checks for orders $9$ through $20$, where this tree gives the second-largest value after the path; a general proof is not provided.
title: The second-largest 1-nearly independent edge-subset count
source_references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.17154

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).
technical_disposition: All forests of every n>=12 and uniqueness are required. A transfer recurrence for one branching tree would not prove global second extremality; the path-gluing convention also needs primary definitions.

statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$) be a minimal Cayley graph, and let $alpha(G)$ denote the size of its largest independent set. 

**Babai's conjecture.** For every $varepsilon>0$, there exists a minimal Cayley graph $G=(V,E)$ such that

$$
\alpha(G) \leq \varepsilon|V|.
$$

This conjecture, mentioned by Babai in connection with the chromatic number of minimal Cayley graphs, would imply minimal Cayley graphs with arbitrarily large chromatic number. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.
title: Babai's independence-ratio conjecture for minimal Cayley graphs
source_references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.19543

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2024). “On the other hand, it also remains open if graphs with a one popular color coloring exist that satisfy Conjecture .”
technical_disposition: The existential graph must work for each epsilon, with a minimal generating set. Generic high-chromatic Cayley graphs do not preserve minimality, so no full constructive mechanism is supplied.

statement:
Let $\mu$ be a log-concave probability measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $\|f\|_{\psi_2(\mu)}$ denote the sub-Gaussian Orlicz norm defined by the best constant $C$ such that

$$
\mu(|f|\geq r)\leq 2\exp\left(-\frac{r^2}{C^2}\right).
$$

Let $D_n$ be the largest log-Sobolev constant among log-concave measures satisfying $\|x\cdot\theta\|_{\psi_2(\mu)}\leq 1$ for every direction $\theta$.

**Log-Sobolev KLS conjecture.**

$$
D_n=O(1).
$$

Equivalently, in the log-concave setting, the log-Sobolev constant should be bounded by the largest squared $\psi_2$-norm of a linear function. This is presented as the log-Sobolev analogue of the KLS conjecture; the source does not specify whether it has been resolved.
title: Log-Sobolev KLS conjecture
source_references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.01324

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).
technical_disposition: Uniformity in dimension over every normalized log-concave measure is essential. One-dimensional or product inequalities are not a full log-Sobolev KLS bound.

statement:
Let a partially ordered family be a family equipped with a partial order. For two elements, a **quasi-supremum** is a minimal upper bound and a **quasi-minimum** is a maximal lower bound. **Lattice characterization conjecture.** A partially ordered family is a lattice if and only if each pair of its elements has a unique quasi-supremum and a unique quasi-minimum.

This asks whether the existence and uniqueness of quasi-suprema and quasi-infima for every pair characterizes lattices. The forward implication follows from the definitions of supremum and infimum; the converse is presented as an open question in the source.
title: Characterization of lattices by unique quasi-suprema and quasi-infima
source_references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.02747

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).
technical_disposition: Definition 4.3 and Conjecture A in the primary match unique minimal upper/maximal lower bounds for every pair. Finite posets cannot witness a failure; an infinite example must satisfy both uniqueness conditions globally. No such checked example is supplied; do not confuse minimal and least.

statement:
Let $cDelta\textgreater=1$. There exists a constant $C_cDelta>0$ such that, whenever $cfrac{C_cDelta}{n}le ple0.1$, the binomial random graph $G(n,p)$ contains, with high probability, every tree of maximum degree at most $cDelta$ and of order

$$
\Omega\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\frac{\log(pn)}{p}\aftergroup\egroup\originalright).
$$

**Large induced bounded-degree trees conjecture.** For every $cDelta\textgreater=1$, the stated containment holds for all such $p$.

This conjecture proposes essentially tight bounds for large induced bounded-degree trees in random graphs. The source presents it as a prospective application of the paper's methods and gives no resolution.
title: Large induced bounded-degree trees conjecture for random graphs
source_references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.04260

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2024).
technical_disposition: The displayed formula and status conflict; induced containment is critical. A non-induced bounded-degree tree embedding would not settle the intended range p~1/n through constant p, uniformly over trees.

statement:
Let $n\ge3$. For integers $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, write $\operatorname{rad}(x_1x_2\cdots x_n)$ for the largest positive squarefree divisor of their product. **The n-terms abc conjecture.** There is a number $M_n$ depending only on $n$ such that, given integers $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ satisfying

$$
\gcd(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=1,\qquad x_1+\cdots+x_n=0,
$$

and such that no proper subsum in the second relation vanishes, one has

$$
\max_{1\le j\le n}|x_j|\le \operatorname{rad}(x_1x_2\cdots x_n)^{M_n}.
$$

Browkin and Brzeziński proposed this extension of the abc conjecture to $n$ terms. The source also records the sharper expected choice $M_n=2n-5+\epsilon$ for every $\epsilon>0$, up to finitely many exceptions; no resolution status is supplied.
title: Browkin–Brzeziński's n-terms abc conjecture
source_references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.05083

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).
technical_disposition: The n=3 specialization already asks for a weak abc bound. Nonvanishing proper subsums and a bound uniform over all tuples prevent a finite certificate or a simple cancellation construction.

statement:
Let $n\ge3$. For non-zero integers $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, write $\operatorname{rad}(x_1x_2\cdots x_n)$ for the largest positive squarefree divisor of their product. **The strong n-terms abc conjecture.** There is a number $M_n$ depending only on $n$ such that, given non-zero integers $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ satisfying

$$
\gcd(x_i,x_j)=1\quad\text{for all }i\ne j,
$$

and

$$
x_1+\cdots+x_n=0,
$$

one has

$$
\max_{1\le j\le n}|x_j|\le \operatorname{rad}(x_1x_2\cdots x_n)^{M_n}.
$$

This is a modification of the n-terms abc conjecture discussed in Browkin's work, replacing the global gcd and nonvanishing proper-subsums conditions by pairwise coprimality and nonzero terms. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
title: The strong n-terms abc conjecture
source_references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.05083

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).
technical_disposition: Pairwise coprimality eliminates the obvious cancelling large pairs, and n=3 again contains weak abc. No full bound in all tuple sizes is available.

statement:
For a finite group $G$, let $\operatorname{Irr}(G)$ denote the set of irreducible complex representations up to isomorphism, and let $\operatorname{Conj}(G)$ denote the set of conjugacy classes of $G$. Let $s(G)$ be the sum of all entries in the character table of $G$, and let $\Gamma_e(G)$ be the sum of the entries in the first column, indexed by the identity class; equivalently, it is the sum of the dimensions of the irreducible representations.

**Fields' conjecture.** For all finite groups $G$, 

$$
s(G)\geq \Gamma_e(G).
$$

Moreover, 

$$
s(G)=\Gamma_e(G)
$$

if and only if $G$ is abelian.

The inequality is due to Fields, while the equality characterization strengthens his conjecture. It is known for groups whose column sums are all nonnegative, for finite groups of nilpotency two, and for all groups of order at most $200$; the full assertion remains open.
title: Fields' character table sum lower-bound conjecture
source_references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.06036

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).
technical_disposition: Both a character-sum inequality for every finite group and the iff equality clause are required. Abelian orthogonality only checks the equality direction; small-group tables do not provide a uniform mechanism.

statement: For even $n$, let $\mathcal{D}(n)$ denote the set of square roots of determinants of $n\times n$ Seidel tournament matrices. The source notes that the argument does not establish this without assuming a skew-conference matrix and suspects that this assumption is unnecessary.

statement:
For a finite graph $G$, let $\Theta(G)$ be its threshold number, the smallest positive integer $k$ such that $G$ is a $k$-threshold graph, and let $G^c$ denote its complement.

**Jamison and Sprague's conjecture.** For every integer $k\ge 1$, there is a graph $G$ with

$$
\Theta(G)=2k \quad\text{and}\quad \Theta(G^c)=2k+1.
$$

Jamison and Sprague established that the threshold numbers of a graph and its complement differ by at most one, with the parity determining which value can occur. Chen and Hao gave a partial solution by determining the threshold numbers of complete multipartite graphs whose parts are not small and of their complements; the stated existence claim is resolved according to the supplied status evidence.
title: Jamison and Sprague's threshold-number conjecture for graphs and their complements
source_references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2022–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2212.00745](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.00745).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.12063

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2024).
technical_disposition: Primary Conjecture 1.5 is explicitly confirmed there by Chen-Hao Theorem 1.6. Use k+1 parts of size at least k+2 to get threshold numbers 2k and 2k+1. Public theorem statement defeats a new brief; original Chen-Hao proof body and dependencies were not audited.

statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid with circumference $c$, and let $C_1$ and $C_2$ be skew circuits, meaning that $r(C_1)+r(C_2)=r(C_1\bowtie C_2)$. For disjoint sets, their **linkage** is the minimum connectivity value between them, and they are $t$-linked when this linkage is at least $t$.

**Skew-circuit circumference bound conjecture.** For every nonnegative integer $k$, there exists an integer $alpha(k)$ depending only on $k$ such that, whenever $C_1$ and $C_2$ are $alpha(k)$-linked,

$$
|C_1|+|C_2|\leq 2c-k.
$$

This conjecture seeks a uniform circumference bound for sufficiently highly linked skew circuits. Earlier results establish related bounds for regular and connected matroids, but the corresponding statement for general matroids is open.
title: Skew-circuit circumference bound conjecture
source_references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13861

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).
technical_disposition: A linkage threshold alpha(k) independent of the matroid and the two circuits is required for every k. Checking graphic or regular matroids cannot supply the full arbitrary-matroid statement.

statement:
Let $\mathsf P_d(t)$ denote the polynomial in the motivic formula for Hilbert schemes of $d$ points, and suppose that $\mathsf P_e(t)$ is known for every integer $e$ with $1\leq e<d$. **Half-data conjecture.** For $d>3$, the number of new data required to compute $\mathsf P_d(t)$ is at most

$$
\left\lceil\frac{d-1}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

Here the new data are the motives $[\operatorname{Hilb}^d({\mathbb A}^i)]$ for $i=1,\ldots,\left\lceil(d-1)/2\right\rceil$. This is presented as a motivic refinement of the corresponding bound for higher-dimensional partition numbers.
title: The half-data conjecture for motivic Hilbert-scheme polynomials
source_references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.14321

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2024). “Another open problem is the following.”
technical_disposition: All d>3 and motivic identities, rather than numerical partition counts, are quantified. Interpolation without a proven coefficient constraint does not reduce the required new data to half.

statement: Let $F_n=\langle x_1,\ldots,x_n\rangle$ be the free group on $n$ generators. For a word $w\in F_n$, let $\operatorname{Pr}_w(g)$ be the probability that $w(g_1,\ldots,g_n)=g$ when $(g_1,\ldots,g_n)$ is chosen uniformly from a finite group $G^n$. Call $w$ **profinetely rigid** if every word $u\in F_n$ inducing the same probability measure as $w$ on every finite group is automorphic to $w$. **Amit–Vishne–Shalev conjecture.** Every word in $F_n$, for $n\geq 2$, is profinitely rigid. The conjecture asserts that the induced probability measures of a word on all finite groups determine its orbit under automorphisms of the free group. It remains open in general, although recent developments support it.
title: Amit–Vishne–Shalev conjecture on profinite rigidity of free-group words
source_references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.00789

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2024). “Although the conjecture is still open in general for words in $F_n$, $n \geq 2$, there have been recent developments in its favour.”
technical_disposition: Equality of word measures on every finite group must imply an automorphism for every free-group word. A finite list of test groups cannot certify the universal rigidity conclusion.

statement: For positive integers $n$ and $m$, let $\emph{\textsf{OV}}(n,m)$ denote the Orthogonal Vectors problem: given sets $A=\{x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(n)}\}$ and $B=\{y^{(1)},\ldots,y^{(n)}\}\subset\{0,1\}^m$, determine whether there are $i,j\in[n]$ with $\langle x^{(i)}-y^{(j)}\rangle=0$. **Orthogonal Vectors Conjecture.** For every $\delta>0$, there is $c\ge 1$ such that $\emph{\textsf{OV}}(n,m)$ cannot be solved in $O(n^{2-\delta})$ time on instances with $m=c\log n$. This conjecture is a standard source of conditional fine-grained lower bounds, including reductions to kernel density estimation; its resolution status is not specified in the input.
title: Orthogonal Vectors Conjecture

statement:
Let $P\in\{0,1\}^{k\times l}$ be any forbidden pattern, and let $G(P)$ be its unordered bipartite graph. Let $\operatorname{Ex}(P,n)$ denote the maximum number of ones in an $n\times n$ matrix avoiding $P$, and let $\operatorname{Ex}_{\mathit{Tur}}(G(P),n)$ denote the Turán extremal function of $G(P)$. **Füredi–Hajnal logarithmic conjecture.** One should have

$$
\operatorname{Ex}(P,n)=O\bigl(\operatorname{Ex}_{\mathit{Tur}}(G(P),n)\log n\bigr).
$$

Pach and Tardos refuted this conjecture in 2005, so it is no longer open.
title: Füredi–Hajnal conjecture for arbitrary forbidden patterns
source_references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.02638

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2024).
technical_disposition: The literal statement itself reports a 2005 Pach-Tardos refutation. No proof body was inspected, so do not upgrade to independently audited retirement; no rediscovery investment is justified.

statement:
A tournament is a complete graph whose edges are directed, and a $t$-augmented tournament has $t$ pairs of vertices carrying both directed edges. Let $t(n,H)$ be the minimum $t$ such that every $n$-vertex, $t$-augmented tournament contains a subgraph isomorphic to the tournament $H$. **Shapira–Yuster conjecture.** For every tournament forest $H$, there is a constant $c_H$ such that

$$
t(n,H)=O(n\log^{c_H}n).
$$

This is presented as an analogue of the Pach–Tardos conjecture for augmented tournaments; no resolution is given in the paper.
title: Shapira–Yuster conjecture for tournament forests
source_references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.02638

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2024).
technical_disposition: Each tournament forest needs one exponent governing all n. A few small tournament embeddings do not control arbitrary forests or produce the polylogarithmic augmented-edge bound.

statement: For a graph $H$, $kH$ denotes the disjoint union of $k$ copies of $H$, and a graph is $H$-induced-minor-free if it does not contain $H$ as an induced minor. **The planar induced-minor Erdős–Pósa conjecture.** For each planar graph $H$, there exist a function $f$ and a constant $d$ such that, for every positive integer $k$ and every graph $G$, either $G$ contains $kH$ as an induced minor, or there is a set $X$ of at most $f(k)$ vertices such that $G-B_G(X,d)$ is $H$-induced-minor-free. This is an induced-minor analogue of the planar graph-minor Erdős–Pósa theorem. The source gives a bounded-maximum-degree version using an induced grid-minor theorem, but does not resolve the unrestricted conjecture.
title: The planar induced-minor Erdős–Pósa conjecture

statement: Let $C_n^k$ be the $k$-th power of the cycle on $n$ vertices, and let $\delta(G)$ denote the minimum degree of a graph $G$. **ELW's Hamiltonicity conjecture.** For all integers $n\geq3$ and $k\in [1,n/2]$, every graph $G\subseteq C_n^k$ with $\delta(G)\geq k+1$ is Hamiltonian. This conjecture concerns a sufficient minimum-degree condition for subgraphs of powers of cycles to contain a Hamilton cycle and arises from the study of local resilience in random geometric graphs; its resolution is not given here.

statement:
Let $P_n^k$ be the $k$-th power of the path on $n$ vertices, and let $\deg_G(v)$ denote the degree of $v$ in $G$. **Hamiltonicity conjecture for path powers.** Let $n\geq4$ and $k\geq2$ be integers. If $G\subseteq P_n^k$ satisfies

$$
\deg_G(v)\geq \deg_{P_n^k}(v)/2+2
$$

for every vertex $v$, then $G$ is Hamiltonian. Motivated by the paper's result for effective minimum degree, this conjecture asks whether preserving slightly more than half the degree of every vertex of a path power guarantees a Hamilton cycle; it would imply the one-dimensional case of the cited random-geometric-graph conjecture and remains open in the source.
title: Hamiltonicity conjecture for subgraphs of powers of paths

statement:
A set of permutations is **quasirandom-forcing** if forcing the corresponding permutation densities determines the uniform measure on $[0,1]^2$. For permutations of arbitrary, possibly different, sizes, the smallest quasirandom-forcing set is known to have cardinality between four and six.

**Minimum size conjecture for permutations.** Every quasirandom-forcing set of permutations has cardinality at least six.

This conjecture asserts that the known upper bound of six is optimal. It strengthens the cited conjecture that no linear combination of six permutations forces quasirandomness.
title: The minimum size conjecture for quasirandom-forcing sets of permutations
source_references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.06869

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}_{d}$ denote the maximum number of vertices of a connected $d$-regular graph with positive Lin–Lu–Yau curvature. For even degree, write $d\in2\mathbb{N}$. **Extremal-size conjecture.** For every $d\in2\mathbb{N}$,

$$
\mathcal{M}_{d}=\sqrt{5}^{d}.
$$

The Cartesian power $(C_{5})^{\square n}$ supplies the lower bound $\mathcal{M}_{d}\geq\sqrt{5}^{d}$ for even $d$ and has constant minimal positive Lin–Lu–Yau curvature. Determining the exact values of $\mathcal{M}_{d}$ for $d\geq4$ remains open.
title: Extremal-size conjecture for regular graphs with positive Lin–Lu–Yau curvature
source_references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.08854

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $k>d\geq 0$, and let $\mathcal{F}\subset\binom{[n]}{k}$ be an **intersecting family**, meaning that any two members of $\mathcal{F}$ have nonempty intersection. Write $\delta_d(\mathcal{F})$ for the minimum $d$-degree of $\mathcal{F}$.

**Minimum-degree conjecture.** For every $k>d\geq 0$ and $n\geq 2k+1$, an intersecting family $\mathcal{F}\subset\binom{[n]}{k}$ always satisfies

$$
\delta_d(\mathcal{F})\leq\binom{n-d-1}{k-d-1}.
$$

The result proved in the paper establishes the corresponding bound for $n\geq 2k+2d-3$. The conjecture is stated to have been verified for $d\in\{0,1,2\}$, while the full range $n\geq 2k+1$ remains open.
title: The minimum-degree conjecture for intersecting uniform families

contains all possible cycle factors; that is, for every such partition, $D$ has $k$ disjoint cycles of lengths $n_1,\ldots,n_k$, respectively. $$
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{F\left(n;\ell,\ell-2\right)}{n^2}.

This is one of the conjectures introduced by Brown, Erdős and Sós concerning extremal numbers for forbidden configurations in $3$-uniform hypergraphs. The source does not state whether the limit has been proved to exist, so its status is recorded as open.

statement:
Let $t>3$ and let $k$ and $n$ be integers satisfying $k>\frac{t}{3}$ and $n>t-1$. A graph is **$K_t$-minor free** if it has no minor isomorphic to the complete graph $K_t$. For some $\lambda\in[1/3,1)$, the following should hold for all such integers $t$, $k$, and $n$:

**Wood's conjecture.** The number of $k$-cliques in a $K_t$-minor free graph on $n$ vertices is at most

$$
\binom{t-2}{k}+(n-t+2)\binom{t-2}{k-1}=\binom{t-2}{k-1}\left(n-\frac{(k-1)(t-1)}{k}\right).
$$

The conjecture proposes an asymptotically sharp upper bound for large clique orders in graphs excluding a complete-graph minor. It extends the exact result for $(t-1)$-cliques, where the maximum is $n-t+2$, and concerns the range in which $k$ is larger than a fixed fraction of $t$; its resolution is not given here.

statement:
Let $r\geq 2$, let $H$ be an $n$-vertex linear $(r+1)$-uniform hypergraph of maximum degree $d\geq 1$, and let $\mathcal{I}(H)$ denote its independent sets. For $I\in\mathcal{I}(H)$ sampled uniformly, write $\partial_r I$ for the relevant $r$-boundary of $I$. **Boundary-size conjecture.** There exists a constant $C_r>0$ such that

$$
\mathrm{E}(|\partial_r I|)\leq C_r\,d\,\alpha(H)^r n^{1-r}.
$$

The conjecture concerns the missing upper bound on the expected boundary size of a uniformly selected independent set in a locally sparse or linear hypergraph. The source says it may be independently interesting, but gives no resolution.
title: Boundary-size conjecture for random independent sets in linear hypergraphs

technical_disposition: The exact r-boundary is not defined in the record. Expected boundary versus alpha(H)^r times d n^(1-r) for every linear hypergraph needs structural control; ordinary edge counting alone is insufficient.

statement:
For a positive speed set $V=\{v_1,\dots,v_n\}$, let $t_0$ be the smallest time in $(0,1)$ at which the origin is lonely, and normalize time by the slowest speed by setting

$$
\hat t_0=t_0v_1.
$$

**Timely Lonely Runner Conjecture.** For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ there is $N$ such that, for every $n$-set $V$ of positive speeds,

$$
\hat t_0\leq N.
$$

The conjecture strengthens the Lonely Runner Conjecture by asserting a bound depending only on the number of runners. The source states that Rifford proved it for $n\leq5$; its general case remains open.
title: Rifford's Timely Lonely Runner Conjecture
source_references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.20160

technical_disposition: Uniform normalized loneliness time for every positive speed set contains the lonely-runner existence issue. Primary survey Conjecture 28 gives n<=5 only and discusses a conditional finite-reduction route; that does not provide a full proof.

statement:
Let $V$ be an $n$-set of positive integer speeds, let $v_n$ denote the largest speed, and let $\|x\|$ be the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer. **Conjecture on lonely times.** For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and every such $V$, there is a positive integer $M$ such that, if

$$
t=\frac{M}{2^{\lceil\ln_2v_n+1\rceil}(n+1)v_n},
$$

then

$$
\min_{v\in V}\|tv\|\geq\frac{1}{n+1}.
$$

The conjecture proposes a structured time at which the origin is lonely and is described in the source as supported by simulations. Its general status is open.
title: Bhardwaj–Narayanan–Venkataraman conjecture on lonely times
source_references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.20160

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2024).
technical_disposition: Primary survey Conjecture 29 matches the structured denominator exactly. An executed exact interval calculation tested 1585 distinct speed sets of sizes 1..5 from 1..12, with zero grid misses and 29 singleton-only cases. This neither resolves all n nor handles general tight isolated times; no new hypothesis brief is justified.

statement:
For two complete graphs, write $R(5,5)$ for the smallest $n$ such that every red-blue edge-coloring of $K_n$ contains a monochromatic copy of $K_5$. The currently known bounds are

$$
43\le R(5,5)\le 46.
$$

**McKay and Radziszowski's conjecture.**

$$
R(5,5)=43.
$$

The conjecture was supported by experimental evidence, while the source records only the bounds $43\le R(5,5)\le46$ and does not provide a resolution.
title: McKay and Radziszowski's conjecture for the Ramsey number $R(5,5)$
source_references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2019–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2212.12630](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.12630), [arXiv:1901.03622](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.03622).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.01549

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).
technical_disposition: The equality R(5,5)=43 requires excluding every 43-vertex Ramsey coloring or supplying a larger lower-bound witness to refute it. No candidate coloring or tractable complete exclusion certificate is available; no large SAT enumeration attempted.
